ai.title: Update SDK readme with API key instructions
ai.summary: The `sdk/README.md` now directs users to create a Codebuff account and get an API key directly from the profile page. The previous instructions to install the CLI and run `codebuff login` to read credentials from the local filesystem have been removed. Code examples now use `process.env.CODEBUFF_API_KEY` instead of parsing `~/.config/manicode/credentials.json`.

eli5.text: If you use the Codebuff tools in your own project, you no longer need to install the command-line assistant and log in through it to access your account. Instead, you now create an account at Codebuff.com, copy your API key from your profile page, and paste it directly into your project's settings using a plain text label. The old step-by-step guide that walked you through installing software and reading a hidden configuration file has been removed and replaced with simpler instructions.

ai.title: Eval runner skips setmessages tool calls
ai.summary: CodebuffRunner in evals/git-evals/runners/codebuff.ts filters out tool_call events where toolCallId equals 'set_messages'. Prevents internal message-state updates from polluting captured tool-call traces during eval runs. Scope limited to the Codebuff eval runner. Import ordering cleaned up alongside the logic change.

eli5.text: When the internal evaluation system watches the assistant solve coding tasks, it now quietly ignores brief bookkeeping messages that the assistant uses to update its own scratch notes. You won't notice anything different while using the assistant; this only affects the behind-the-scenes recordings that engineers use to score how well the assistant performed.

ai.title: Trim prompt logging in websocket-action.ts
ai.summary: Prompt logging now truncates to 100 chars and passes structured metadata. `logger.info` call updated in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`. Reduces log noise from large prompts. Internal change only.

eli5.text: When you type a message to the assistant over a WebSocket connection, the system used to write your full prompt into its log files, which could be very long. Now it logs only the first 100 characters of what you typed, plus some structured data, so the logs stay smaller and easier to read. This change is already live and only affects what the system records for its own debugging purposes; you see no difference in how your messages are delivered.

ai.title: SDK v0.1.17 adds API key retrieval and custom tools
ai.summary: Version bump to 0.1.17 in @codebuff/sdk. Adds support for retrieving API keys via Codebuff website and providing custom tools. Updates types and documentation.

eli5.text: You can now sign into the Codebuff website and generate your own personal API key to connect to the service, instead of needing one handed to you. If you're building with the toolkit, you can also plug in your own custom tools to make the assistant do specific tasks tailored to your project. The release also updated the reference guide so the instructions match the new options available.

ai.title: Revert eval prompting to Vercel AI SDK
ai.summary: Reverts `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` to use `promptAiSdkStructured` instead of `CodebuffClient` for agent prompting. Removes SDK client initialization, `getUserCredentials` imports, and explicit `sdkClient.closeConnection` calls. Directly invokes `@codebuff/backend/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk` with `models.gemini2_5_flash` and `AgentDecisionSchema`.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes system that checks whether the coding assistant is doing its job got swapped back to an older, simpler method of asking the assistant what to do next. The team noticed the newer method they had tried was causing problems in the test environment, so they flipped it back to the version that was working before. If you watched the internal testing process run, you would see it take the same path through the evaluation as it did before, and the more complex setup step involving creating a separate connection object has been removed entirely.

ai.title: Add CodebuffMessage Zod schemas
ai.summary: New CodebuffMessage types in common/src/types/messages/codebuff-message.ts, replacing legacy schema in session-state.ts. Includes content-part, data-content, provider-metadata, and json.ts. Tool call string logic in tools/utils.ts now defaults endsAgentStep to false if undefined.

eli5.text: The assistant now has a new, more precise way of understanding the different types of messages it sends and receives, kind of like upgrading a filing system so each note is sorted by a clearer, stricter label. This affects the core messaging layer, so anyone working with the assistant's message-handling internals (such as developers extending the agent or tooling) benefits from fewer mismatches and more predictable data shapes. Because the new message types replace the older ones across multiple files, the project becomes easier to refactor and less likely to break when adding new message parts such as images, files, or structured reasoning. ai.title: base2 agent relies on sub-agents and adds step limit
ai.summary: Added 'Rely on agents' and 'Don't mastermind' instructions to base2 factory prompts, directing the orchestrator to delegate planning and execution to spawned sub-agents rather than reading code sections itself. Introduced a maxSteps=10 guard in handleSteps: when the step limit is hit, an add_message tool call injects a user prompt forcing the agent to summarize progress and end its turn. Change isolated to .agents/base2/base2-factory.ts, affecting internal orchestration logic without altering user-facing CLI or Web surfaces.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that coordinates coding tasks now delegates more of the actual planning and code-reading to the smaller helper agents it spawns, rather than trying to inspect files itself. At the same time, that coordinator is given an internal stopwatch: once it has taken roughly ten turns, it automatically stops and asks for a progress summary so it doesn't run endlessly. These two edits live in the coordination logic that runs behind the scenes, so the public command-line and web tools you interact with look and behave exactly the same.

ai.title: Revert session state to CodebuffMessageSchema
ai.summary: Session state imports `CodebuffMessageSchema` from `./message` instead of `codebuffMessageSchema` from `./messages/codebuff-message`. Reverts recent schema path and casing changes in `common/src/types/session-state.ts`. Affects core shared types for agent session persistence. `AgentStateSchema.messageHistory` array type now references the original schema export.

eli5.text: The software that remembers your conversation history between sessions now uses the original naming for how it stores each message. This only affects developers working on the core files that save and load your past chats; regular users will not notice anything different. The change simply switches one import name and two references back to what they were before.

ai.title: 30-minute timeout added to git eval tasks
ai.summary: runGitEvals wraps individual commit eval promises in withTimeout at 30 minutes (60_000 * 30). Prevents hung eval tasks from blocking the concurrency limiter indefinitely. Change scoped to evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts. Timeout applies per-commit, inside the pLimit(20) concurrency boundary.

eli5.text: When the system runs automated tests that check how the assistant behaves on specific code examples, each individual test now stops on its own after 30 minutes if it gets stuck, instead of running forever and blocking other tests. This means the queue of tests keeps moving even if one example hangs, but each test still only gets 30 minutes to finish before it's cut off. Nothing about the results changes for tests that finish normally; they just can't freeze the whole batch anymore.

ai.title: Remove legacy Message type and transformMessages
ai.summary: Codebase now exclusively uses `CodebuffMessage` from `@codebuff/common/types/messages/codebuff-message`. The legacy `Message` type and `transformMessages` utility in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` were deleted, removing ~100 lines of conversion logic. Imports across backend services (`relabelRuns`, `fast-rewrite`, `gemini-with-fallbacks`, etc.) updated to the new path. `saveAgentRequest` debugging helper removed.

eli5.text: The software now uses a single, updated way of packaging conversations with the AI assistant, replacing an older, now-deleted method that translated between formats. If you looked at the code, you'd notice every part of the system that sends or receives messages now imports from the same shared message type. This is live today for anyone running version zero point one point seventeen of the tool, which includes the new message format along with instructions for setting up API keys and custom tools.

ai.title: Refactor sessions route with helpers and add error logging
ai.summary: The DELETE /api/sessions endpoint in web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts was refactored to extract revokeStandardSessions and revokeApiTokens helpers. Session revocation now handles raw tokens or sha256 hashes, restricts deletion to web/cli types, and unclaims CLI fingerprints within a transaction. PAT revocation remains separate. The catch block now logs errors via logger.error before returning 500.

eli5.text: You can now sign out of specific web or desktop sessions without affecting your API keys: the sign-out tool was reorganized so each job does one clear thing. When you request a session be revoked, the system matches your request whether you pasted the raw token or its secret fingerprint, then removes only web/desktop sessions and releases any linked device fingerprints in the same safe step. If something goes wrong during sign-out, the error is now recorded for troubleshooting instead of being silently dropped, and API key revocation stays in its own separate step.

ai.title: Confirmation dialog input clear via useEffect
ai.summary: ConfirmationInputDialog in `web/src/components/ui/confirmation-input-dialog.tsx` clears `inputValue` via `useEffect` on `isOpen` change. Replaces redundant `setInputValue('')` call in `handleOpenChange`. Internal refactor for consistent state management.

eli5.text: When you close a confirmation dialog that asks you to type text to confirm an action, the typed text now clears automatically. The system uses a single automatic cleanup step that runs when the dialog is closed, instead of two separate cleanup attempts that did the same thing. For you, the dialog behaves the same way: close it and the input is empty next time. The change only affects how the clearing happens behind the scenes.

ai.title: Profile sign-in gate and SDK doc update
ai.summary: Profile page now gates on auth status, rendering `ProfileLoggedOut` card for unauthenticated users instead of empty state. `SignInButton` accepts optional `onClick` for analytics and preserves `referral_code` in localStorage during non-login flows. SDK README prerequisites condensed to single line linking API keys page. Covers `web/src/app/profile` components and `sdk/README.md`.

eli5.text: If you visit your profile page without being signed in, you now see a helpful "Sign in to Codebuff" card with a button to log in, instead of a blank or confusing page. The sign-in button has been improved to optionally track when people click it for analytics purposes, and it now preserves referral codes when you're signing in through other flows. The setup instructions for developers using the software development kit have also been simplified to a single clear line that links directly to where you get your API key. These changes are live today and affect anyone visiting the profile page while not logged in, as well as developers following the SDK setup guide.

ai.title: Replace custom patch implementation with diff library
ai.summary: Deleted custom `applyPatch` logic in `common/src/util/patch.ts` and migrated to `diff` library (v8.0.2) for both `npm-app` and `sdk`. Added explicit error handling for failed patches (`newContent === false`) in `npm-app/src/utils/changes.ts` and `sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts`. Removed unused `applyAndRevertChanges` function.

eli5.text: You won't see a new feature, but the assistant's behind-the-scenes machinery for editing your files just got simpler and more reliable. The team deleted their hand-written patch code, the thing that figures out how to merge suggested changes into your existing files, and replaced it with a widely-used off-the-shelf library called diff. That swap is live today for the desktop app and the programmable toolkit, and the two spots that actually apply your file edits now also explicitly catch and report the rare case where a change can't be merged instead of failing silently.
